reference.source: Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System / RCOG Green-top Guideline
clinicalPearls: Presents in the second or third trimester with intense pruritus, classically of the palms and soles, in the absence of a primary skin rash
The diagnostic hallmark is raised fasting serum bile acids; transaminases may also be mildly elevated
Jaundice is uncommon; itch typically precedes biochemical change and resolves within days to weeks after delivery
The principal concern is fetal risk: spontaneous preterm birth, meconium-stained liquor, and, with high bile acid levels, an increased risk of stillbirth
Susceptibility is influenced by heterozygous variants in biliary transporter genes, notably ABCB4 (MDR3), and by oestrogen and progesterone metabolites
It tends to recur in subsequent pregnancies and with combined oestrogen-containing contraception

Management centres on ursodeoxycholic acid for maternal symptoms, fetal monitoring, and planned delivery timed according to bile acid levels and gestation, with vitamin K if there is prolonged cholestasis or coagulopathy
reference.pathophysiology: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is a reversible, hormonally influenced cholestasis of late pregnancy. Rising oestrogen and progesterone metabolites impair hepatocellular bile acid transport in genetically susceptible women, many of whom carry heterozygous variants in canalicular transporter genes such as ABCB4 (MDR3), ABCB11 (BSEP), or ATP8B1. Reduced canalicular excretion raises circulating bile acids, causing maternal pruritus; transplacental passage of elevated bile acids is implicated in fetal complications including arrhythmia, preterm birth, and sudden intrauterine death, with risk rising steeply at very high maternal bile acid concentrations. The condition characteristically resolves after delivery.
additionalDifferentials: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP)
Pemphigoid gestationis and atopic eruption of pregnancy
Viral hepatitis or drug-induced liver injury
Primary biliary cholangitis presenting in pregnancy
additionalInvestigations: Fasting serum bile acid concentration (key test, guiding severity and delivery timing)
Liver function tests including transaminases and bilirubin
Coagulation profile and vitamin K status if cholestasis is prolonged
Viral hepatitis serology and liver autoantibodies to exclude other causes
Liver and biliary ultrasound to exclude obstruction
Fetal surveillance including cardiotocography and growth assessment
redFlags: Very high maternal serum bile acids indicating heightened stillbirth risk
Reduced fetal movements or abnormal cardiotocography
Jaundice, right upper quadrant pain, or features suggesting acute fatty liver or pre-eclampsia
Coagulopathy from vitamin K deficiency in prolonged cholestasis
Persistent abnormal liver tests beyond the postpartum period suggesting underlying liver disease
reference.prognosis: Maternal prognosis is excellent with resolution of pruritus and biochemistry after delivery, though recurrence in future pregnancies is common; the main determinant of outcome is fetal, with planned delivery and bile-acid-guided monitoring aimed at reducing the risk of stillbirth.
pitfalls: Reassuring on the basis of mild itch without measuring serum bile acids
Overlooking the rising stillbirth risk at very high bile acid concentrations when planning delivery
Failing to exclude pre-eclampsia, HELLP, or acute fatty liver of pregnancy
Not arranging postpartum follow-up to confirm resolution and detect underlying liver disease
Neglecting vitamin K when cholestasis is prolonged, risking maternal or neonatal bleeding
references: Sherlock's Diseases of the Liver and Biliary System
RCOG Green-top Guideline on intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
management: Give ursodeoxycholic acid to relieve maternal pruritus and lower serum bile acids
Provide symptomatic relief of itch with emollients and a sedating antihistamine at night
Supplement vitamin K where cholestasis is prolonged or coagulation is deranged
Monitor fasting serum bile acids and liver function serially to gauge severity and guide delivery timing
Undertake foetal surveillance and plan early delivery timed to bile-acid concentration to reduce stillbirth risk
Avoid oestrogen-containing contraception postpartum given recurrence risk, and confirm biochemical resolution after delivery
Coordinate obstetric and hepatology care, with genetic counselling where a biliary transporter variant such as ABCB4 (MDR3) is identified
